newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA sees wage growth pressure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA sees wage growth pressure.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Tuesday that it had kept wages growth down in the past but that this would inevitably rise because of higher inflation.

CBA managing director David Murray told the bank's annual meeting in Melbourne that the CBA had restricted wage increases to four percent in the two years prior to the most recently negotiated round of enterprise bargaining agreements.

"That is clearly not sustainable with the inflation rate and wage expectations where they are but we continue to bargain hard on that front," Murray said in response to a question about costs and future profitability.
In March this year, the bank said it had agreed with the Finance Sector Union on pay increases of up to 11 percent for staff in the period to June 1997.

Murray had been asked by one shareholder why CBA's staff costs had risen by more than five percent in 1995/96 when staff number had risen by less than one percent. He said this was because of increased overtime costs and increased provisioning for long service leave and other staff leave.
He was also asked why CBA's aggregate cost to revenue ratio remained among the highest in Australian banking at about 61 percent.
Murray said CBA's costs were higher because it was more focussed on the retail side of banking, but the bank still wanted to reduce the ratio further.
"We are not complacent at all about that ratio," he said.

CBA chairman Tim Besley earlier told shareholders the bank had previously predicted that 1996/97 earnings would be flat and the first three months of the current year did not require any change to this scenario.
